# =============================================================================
# Harmonia Experiment Failure Mode Taxonomy
# =============================================================================
# Schema version: 1.1
# Date: 25 February 2026 (added 2F: Model Pre-load Timeout, 3H: Ollama Silent Context Truncation)
#
# This file defines the problem classes that the CLI log/trace analysis tool
# uses to categorize experiment failures. Each problem class has:
#   - id: unique identifier (category_number + letter)
#   - category: high-level grouping
#   - name: short descriptive name
#   - description: full explanation
#   - severity: critical | error | warning | info
#   - detection: keyword/regex patterns to search for in logs and traces
#   - example: real snippet from a log or trace
#   - remediation: list of suggested fixes
#
# COMPOUND DETECTION LOGIC:
# Some problem classes require compound conditions (e.g., "all turns timeout
# AND raw_messages count <= 1 per turn"). These cannot be expressed as simple
# keyword/regex patterns. They are implemented in Python in the CLI tool
# (see _detect_* methods). This YAML only contains the simple patterns;
# compound logic is documented in comments under each relevant problem class.
#
# See also: documentation/processes/11_02_2026_interpreting_logs_and_traces.md
# =============================================================================

schema_version: "1.0"

problem_classes:

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 1: Infrastructure / Beaker Server Failures
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "1A"
    category: "infrastructure"
    name: "Beaker Server Hung"
    description: |
      The Beaker server becomes unresponsive after processing a previous batch
      of experiment runs. All 8 turns timeout with an identical, deterministic
      duration pattern [180, 300, 180, 180, 360, 600, 300, 120] totaling exactly
      2220 seconds. Each turn's raw_messages contains only a single status:busy
      message — the Beaker kernel never starts processing.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_beaker_server_hung):
      #   1. ALL turns have response_type == "timeout"
      #   2. Each turn has <= 1 raw_message
      #   3. Total duration is approximately 2220 seconds (± 30s)
      # These conditions together distinguish infrastructure hang from
      # LLM-side timeouts (3A), where raw_messages count > 1 per turn.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      # 1A detection is PURELY compound (Python-only). No simple keywords,
      # because "Request timed out after" also appears in 3A (LLM-side timeout).
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "turn": 1,
          "agent_response": "Request timed out after 180.0 seconds",
          "response_type": "timeout",
          "tool_calls": [],
          "duration_seconds": 180.001,
          "raw_messages": [
            {
              "msg_type": "status",
              "content": { "execution_state": "busy" }
            }
          ]
        }
    remediation:
      - "Restart Beaker between runs: modify run_experiment.py to restart the Beaker server (or kernel) between experiment runs"
      - "Detect hung server: send a health-check request (GET /api/sessions) before sending turns; abort if no response within 10s"
      - "Limit retries: only attempt one run per Beaker server instance, or restart server between retries"

  - id: "1B"
    category: "infrastructure"
    name: "405 Method Not Allowed on Notebook Save"
    description: |
      Beaker returns HTTP 405 when attempting to save a notebook. This appears
      in almost all SLURM .out logs as a warning but does not crash the experiment.
      Beaker's dev mode tries to auto-save notebooks, but the API doesn't support
      PUT for this path.
    severity: "info"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "405 PUT /api/contents/notebook.ipynb"
      log_regex:
        - "\\d+ PUT /api/contents/.*\\.ipynb"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        [W 2026-02-10 19:34:33.506 BeakerServerApp] 405 PUT /api/contents/notebook.ipynb (::1) 0.74ms referer=None
    remediation:
      - "Ignore: this is a non-fatal warning that does not affect experiment results"
      - "Suppress in logging: configure Beaker's logging level to suppress 405 warnings"
      - "Fix Beaker config: configure the correct save endpoint if notebook saving is desired"

  - id: "1C"
    category: "infrastructure"
    name: "ZMQ ReadTimeout on Context Cleanup"
    description: |
      After the experiment completes, the Beaker kernel's cleanup process
      encounters a ZMQ ReadTimeout when trying to tear down the context.
      This appears in the SLURM .out log at the very end and does not affect
      experiment results.
    severity: "info"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "Uncaught exception in ZMQStream callback"
        - "zmq.error.ZMQError"
      log_regex:
        - "ZMQ.*[Tt]imeout"
        - "Uncaught exception in ZMQStream"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        Uncaught exception in ZMQStream callback
        Traceback (most recent call last):
          File ".../zmq/eventloop/zmqstream.py", line 565, in _log_error
            f.result()
          File ".../beaker_kernel/lib/jupyter_kernel_proxy.py", line 253, in handler
          ...
          File ".../beaker_kernel/kernel.py", line 550, in llm_request
            result = await task
    remediation:
      - "Ignore: occurs during cleanup after the experiment finishes; does not affect results"
      - "Graceful shutdown: implement a proper shutdown sequence that sends a kernel shutdown request before disconnecting"
      - "Catch and suppress: wrap the Beaker kernel's cleanup handler in try/except"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 2: Model Configuration / Availability Errors
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "2A"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "Ollama Model Not Found"
    description: |
      The Ollama API returns HTTP 404 because the requested model name does not
      match any installed model. The model is either misspelled or not pulled.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex:
        - "model '.*' not found"
        - "ResponseError.*not found.*status code: 404"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        ollama._types.ResponseError: model 'olmo-3.1:32b' not found (status code: 404)
    remediation:
      - "Fix model name in config YAML to match an installed model; verify with 'ollama list'"
      - "Add model validation to exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh: verify requested model exists after Ollama starts"
      - "Import custom model from HuggingFace GGUF: 'ollama create <name> -f Modelfile'"

  - id: "2B"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "Tool Calling Not Supported"
    description: |
      The LLM framework (Archytas/LangChain) raises a ValueError because the
      model's Ollama template does not declare tool support. Ollama determines
      tool support by checking if the model's Go template references {{ .Tools }}.
      The model may actually support tool calling natively, but the Ollama template
      is missing the required block.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "does not support tool calling"
        - "does not support tool"
      log_regex:
        - "ValueError.*does not support tool"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        ValueError: Model 'kimi-k2' does not support tool calling
    remediation:
      - "Use community model with tool template: e.g., 'ollama pull huihui_ai/kimi-k2'"
      - "Create custom Modelfile that adds {{ .Tools }} template block"
      - "Check if ValueError comes from Ollama or from Archytas/LangChain pre-checking; add to allowlist if client-side"

  - id: "2C"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "Ollama Runner Process Crash"
    description: |
      The Ollama runner subprocess crashes with exit status 2 during model
      inference. This is an Ollama-internal error, typically related to model
      loading, GGUF format issues, or GPU memory exhaustion.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "llama runner process has terminated"
        - "exit status 2"
      log_regex:
        - "llama runner.*exit status \\d+"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        llama runner process has terminated: exit status 2
    remediation:
      - "Check model integrity: re-pull the model with 'ollama pull <model>'"
      - "Check GPU memory: use 'seff <jobid>' to check memory usage; try smaller quantization or more VRAM"
      - "Check Ollama version compatibility: some models require newer Ollama versions"

  - id: "2D"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "OpenRouter Model No Longer Available"
    description: |
      The OpenRouter API returns HTTP 404 indicating that a free-tier model's
      free period has ended and the model must be accessed via a paid slug.
      All turns complete in <1 second (the API error is immediate) and
      total experiment duration is typically <10s.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "period has ended"
        - "migrate to the paid slug"
      trace_regex:
        - "free.*period has ended"
        - "migrate to the paid slug"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        LLM Error:
            Error from OpenRouter: {'error': {'message': 'The free MiMo-V2-Flash period has ended. To continue using this model, please migrate to the paid slug: xiaomi/mimo-v2-flash', 'code': 404}}
    remediation:
      - "Remove from roster: delete the config YAML for models that are no longer free"
      - "Switch to paid slug: update config to use paid model slug with sufficient OpenRouter credits"
      - "Add availability check: make lightweight API call before experiment to verify model is accessible"

  - id: "2E"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "OpenRouter Rate Limit Exceeded"
    description: |
      The OpenRouter API returns HTTP 429 when the free-tier rate limit is
      exceeded. Free models are typically limited to 20 requests/minute.
      First 1-2 turns may succeed, then subsequent turns return empty responses
      very quickly (<1s).
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "Rate limit exceeded"
        - "rate limit"
      trace_regex:
        - "'code': 429"
        - "Rate limit exceeded.*free-models"
        - "X-RateLimit-Remaining.*0"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        LLM Error:
            Error from OpenRouter: {'error': {'message': 'Rate limit exceeded: free-models-per-min. ', 'code': 429, 'metadata': {'headers': {'X-RateLimit-Limit': '20', 'X-RateLimit-Remaining': '0'}}}}
    remediation:
      - "Add rate limiting: implement configurable delay between turns (3-5s for free models at 20 req/min)"
      - "Implement retry with backoff: parse X-RateLimit-Reset header and wait before retrying"
      - "Use paid tier: paid OpenRouter plans have significantly higher rate limits"

  - id: "2F"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "Model Pre-load Timeout (Beaker Never Started)"
    description: |
      The Ollama model pre-loading step in exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh exceeds the
      MAX_WAIT timeout (default 300s). The pre-load curl to /api/generate blocks
      while Ollama loads the model into GPU/CPU memory and runs a warm-up inference.
      Beaker never starts because the script is still waiting on the pre-load.
      The sbatch wrapper's readiness poll gives up and kills everything.

      Three root causes observed:
      1. Model saturates GPU VRAM (e.g., 24 GB model on 24 GB GPU) causing
         partial CPU offload and extremely slow loading.
      2. Very large model file (e.g., 31 GB Q8_0) takes too long to read from
         NFS and load into GPU memory, even with sufficient VRAM.
      3. GPU contention: two SLURM GPU jobs land on the same node/GPU, and the
         first model to load consumes all VRAM, starving the second.

      Distinguishing signature: SLURM .out log contains "Pre-loading model: <name>"
      but never "Model preloaded successfully". No results directory is created.
      No trace.json exists. The ollama log shows model loading started but never
      completed.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "Pre-loading model"
      log_regex:
        - "Pre-loading model:.*"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (not yet implemented):
      #   1. Log contains "Pre-loading model:" but NOT "Model preloaded successfully"
      #   2. No results directory exists for this run
      #   3. No trace.json found
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        GPU 0: Tesla V100-PCIE-16GB (UUID: GPU-...)
        Starting Ollama server on port 11434 ...
        Ollama server is ready
        Pre-loading model: nemotron-3-nano:30b
        [300 seconds pass, no further output]
        Timeout waiting for Beaker to start
    remediation:
      - "Increase MAX_WAIT from 300s to 600s in sbatch template for larger models (30B+ or Q8_0)"
      - "Match model size to GPU VRAM: avoid loading models that saturate available VRAM (leave 2-4 GB headroom)"
      - "Prevent GPU contention: use SLURM --exclusive or --gres=gpu:1 to ensure single-tenant GPU allocation"
      - "Pre-pull models to local scratch before job starts to avoid NFS bottleneck during loading"
      - "Use smaller quantizations (Q4_K_M instead of Q8_0) for models that are borderline for the GPU"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 3: LLM Behavioral Failures
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "3A"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "LLM-Side Timeout on Complex Tasks"
    description: |
      The LLM responds to simple prompts (data loading, basic questions) but
      stalls/times out on complex analytical tasks (schema matching, value
      mapping). The model is running but takes too long to generate a response.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_llm_side_timeout):
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "timeout"
      #   2. Turn has > 1 raw_message (differentiates from 1A infrastructure hang)
      #   3. raw_messages include beaker__execute_input or stream messages
      #      (the kernel IS processing, but the LLM is slow)
      #   4. Other turns in the same experiment may have succeeded
      # This distinguishes from 1A where ALL turns timeout with exactly 1
      # raw_message each.
      # 3A detection is PURELY compound (Python-only). No simple keywords,
      # because "Request timed out after" also appears in 1A (Beaker hung).
      # The compound logic checks raw_message count > 1 per timeout turn.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        Turn 1: response_type=llm_response, duration=16.8s (success)
        Turn 3: response_type=timeout, duration=180.0s, raw_messages=[
          {msg_type: "status", content: {execution_state: "busy"}},
          {msg_type: "beaker__execute_input", ...},
          {msg_type: "stream", ...}
        ]
    remediation:
      - "Increase per-turn timeout from 180s to 600s+ for complex tasks in experiment config"
      - "Simplify prompts: break complex multi-step tasks into smaller, focused turns"
      - "Use faster/larger models: smaller models (<30B) struggle with complex reasoning; try 70B+ or cloud models"

  - id: "3B"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "LLM Not Using Tools / Text-Only Guidance"
    description: |
      The LLM responds to prompts but does NOT use Beaker's code execution
      capabilities. Instead, it outputs text guidance like "here's the Python
      code you could run" or "I can't directly manipulate files." This defeats
      the purpose of the agent framework.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_not_using_tools):
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "llm_response" (not timeout)
      #   2. tool_calls array is empty
      #   3. agent_response contains phrases indicating text-only guidance
      # The keyword detection below catches the most common phrases.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "I don't have the capability"
        - "I can't directly"
        - "here's how you could"
        - "I cannot directly"
        - "you could run"
        - "I'm unable to"
      trace_regex:
        - "(?i)I (?:don't|do not|can't|cannot) (?:have the capability|directly)"
        - "(?i)here'?s (?:how|the code) you could"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "turn": 7,
          "agent_response": "I don't have the capability to directly save files to the filesystem. However, I can guide you through the process...",
          "response_type": "llm_response",
          "tool_calls": [],
          "duration_seconds": 17.0
        }
    remediation:
      - "Improve system prompt: add explicit instructions that the agent MUST use run_code, not just suggest code"
      - "Use models trained for tool use: code-focused models (devstral) may default to explanation over execution"
      - "Modify Archytas agent prompt template in archytas/react.py to emphasize tools MUST be used"

  - id: "3C"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Hallucinated / Fabricated Output Data"
    description: |
      When the source data file is not found (FileNotFoundError), some LLMs
      fabricate output data entirely unrelated to the task rather than reporting
      the error and stopping. The fabricated data often matches the model's
      training data patterns (e.g., project management schemas) rather than
      biomedical data.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_hallucinated_output):
      #   1. metrics.json exists AND column_mapping_accuracy == 0.0
      #   2. extra_columns list contains column names not in GDC schema
      #   3. Often preceded by FileNotFoundError in earlier turns
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "both"
      snippet: |
        // metrics.json showing 0% accuracy with fabricated columns
        {
          "column_mapping_accuracy": 0.0,
          "correct_mappings": 0,
          "total_expected": 11,
          "extra_columns": ["dou_id", "dou_title", "dou_description"]
        }
    remediation:
      - "Fix data path to prevent FileNotFoundError in the first place (see 4A)"
      - "Add data validation: after LLM produces output, verify columns match expected GDC schema"
      - "Add guardrails: check if dou_harmonized.csv contains expected column names before marking run as successful"

  - id: "3D"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "WebSocket Message Size Exceeded"
    description: |
      The LLM generates a response that exceeds the Beaker WebSocket message
      size limit (4MB default), crashing the connection. Typically happens when
      the model tries to process or output the entire GDC schema at once.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "Message size"
        - "exceeds limit"
        - "WebSocketError"
      trace_regex:
        - "Message size \\d+ exceeds limit \\d+"
        - "WebSocketError.*Message size"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "status": "error",
          "error_message": "WebSocketError: Message size 5784393 exceeds limit 4194304"
        }
    remediation:
      - "Increase WebSocket limit: set c.ServerApp.websocket_max_message_size = 20 * 1024 * 1024 (20MB) in Jupyter config"
      - "Chunk large data: break large data (full GDC schema) into smaller chunks across multiple turns"
      - "Limit LLM response length: set max_tokens in LLM config (e.g., 4096 tokens per turn)"

  - id: "3E"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Context Window Exhaustion (API Token Limit Exceeded)"
    description: |
      The accumulated conversation history (system prompt, all prior turns,
      raw_messages, Beaker state introspection) exceeds the model's maximum
      context length. The LLM provider API rejects the request immediately
      with HTTP 400. Once this occurs, every subsequent turn also fails
      because the conversation history only grows. The error is silently
      swallowed by the archytas/toki layer — agent_response is empty and
      response_type is "llm_response" (not "error"), making the failure
      invisible without raw_messages inspection.

      Distinguishing signature: turns complete in <2 seconds, agent_response
      is empty, and raw_messages stderr contains "maximum context length"
      with an explicit token count. The requested token count is typically
      far above the model's limit (e.g., 1,015,000 vs 200,000).
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # Keyword detection catches the API error message in serialized trace text.
      # Compound logic (_detect_context_window_exhaustion) cross-checks:
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "llm_response"
      #   2. agent_response is empty ("")
      #   3. duration_seconds < 2.0 (API rejects instantly)
      #   4. raw_messages contain "maximum context length"
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "maximum context length"
      trace_regex:
        - "maximum context length is \\d+ tokens"
        - "you requested about \\d+ tokens"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        Error from OpenRouter: {'error': {'message': "This endpoint's maximum
        context length is 200000 tokens. However, you requested about 1015152
        tokens (1011709 of text input, 3443 of tool input). Please reduce the
        length of either one, or use the \"middle-out\" transform to compress
        your prompt automatically.", 'code': 400}}
    remediation:
      - "Implement context window monitoring: track approximate token count before each API call and warn at 80% capacity"
      - "Implement conversation summarization or truncation when approaching the model's context limit"
      - "Use provider-specific context compression (e.g., OpenRouter's 'middle-out' transform) if available"
      - "Surface the API error to agent_response instead of silently returning empty"
      - "Reduce Beaker state introspection verbosity: raw_messages include large serialized state objects that inflate context"

  - id: "3F"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Response Stream Truncated (Premature Connection Close)"
    description: |
      The LLM provider begins streaming a response but the HTTP connection
      is severed mid-transfer, resulting in a ChunkedEncodingError or
      ProtocolError from urllib3/requests. The archytas/toki layer catches
      the exception but returns an empty string as the agent_response rather
      than raising an error. The turn is recorded as response_type
      "llm_response" (apparent success) with an empty response.

      Distinguishing signature: duration is significant (tens of seconds,
      indicating real LLM processing occurred), agent_response is empty,
      and raw_messages stderr contains "Response ended prematurely" or
      "ChunkedEncodingError". Differs from 3E (context exhaustion) by
      taking real time and having a network-level error rather than a
      token-count error.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # Keyword detection catches the network error in serialized trace text.
      # Compound logic (_detect_response_stream_truncated) cross-checks:
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "llm_response"
      #   2. agent_response is empty ("")
      #   3. duration_seconds > 5.0 (real processing occurred before stream broke)
      #   4. raw_messages contain "Response ended prematurely" or "ChunkedEncodingError"
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "Response ended prematurely"
        - "ChunkedEncodingError"
      trace_regex:
        - "(?:Response ended prematurely|ChunkedEncodingError)"
        - "ProtocolError.*Response ended prematurely"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        LLM Error:
            Response ended prematurely

            Traceback (most recent call last):
              ...
            urllib3.exceptions.ProtocolError: Response ended prematurely

            During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
              ...
            requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError: Response ended prematurely
    remediation:
      - "Implement retry logic for transient network errors (ChunkedEncodingError is typically transient)"
      - "Surface the error in agent_response rather than silently returning empty"
      - "Add response validation: if agent_response is empty after a non-timeout turn, flag as error"
      - "Set request timeout and connection keep-alive parameters in the HTTP client"

  - id: "3G"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Silent Empty Response (No Agent Output)"
    description: |
      A turn completes with response_type "llm_response" (apparent success)
      but agent_response is empty or whitespace-only. This is a cross-cutting
      detection that catches any case where the LLM framework silently
      swallowed an error. Specific causes include context window exhaustion
      (3E) and response stream truncation (3F), but this class also catches
      unknown error types that result in empty responses.

      When 3E or 3F is also detected for the same run, 3G provides additional
      context (which specific turns were affected). When neither 3E nor 3F
      is detected, 3G flags an undiagnosed silent failure.
    severity: "warning"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_silent_empty_response):
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "llm_response" (not timeout, not error)
      #   2. agent_response is empty or whitespace-only
      #   3. The turn is NOT the last turn (last turn may legitimately be empty)
      # This is purely compound — no keyword/regex patterns.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "turn": 4,
          "agent_response": "",
          "response_type": "llm_response",
          "tool_calls": [],
          "duration_seconds": 0.646
        }
    remediation:
      - "Investigate raw_messages for the affected turn to identify the root cause"
      - "Fix the archytas/toki error handling layer to surface errors in agent_response instead of returning empty"
      - "Add response validation in run_experiment.py: abort or retry if agent_response is empty"
      - "Log empty responses as explicit warnings in the experiment output"

  - id: "3H"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Ollama Silent Context Truncation (num_ctx Mismatch)"
    description: |
      Ollama silently truncates the input prompt to its default num_ctx=4096
      tokens because Beaker/Archytas does not pass the num_ctx parameter on
      /api/chat calls. The OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH setting in .env is only applied
      during the initial model pre-load (/api/generate), not during subsequent
      chat requests.

      This is a SILENT degradation — Ollama still produces output, but the model
      loses earlier conversation history. The only evidence is a WARN-level log
      line in the Ollama log file. The experiment appears to succeed but output
      quality is degraded because the model lacks context from prior turns.

      Severity ranges from minor (devstral overflows by ~300 tokens, losing a
      small prefix) to catastrophic (qwen3-coder overflows by 688,358 tokens,
      meaning 99.4% of the prompt is discarded).

      Distinguishing signature: Ollama log contains "truncating input prompt"
      with limit=4096 and prompt > 4096. The experiment continues normally
      (no errors in trace.json or SLURM logs).
    severity: "warning"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "truncating input prompt"
      log_regex:
        - "truncating input prompt.*limit=\\d+.*prompt=\\d+"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        time=2026-02-10T21:08:41.096+01:00 level=WARN source=runner.go:153
        msg="truncating input prompt" limit=4096 prompt=4200 keep=5 new=4096
    remediation:
      - "Pass num_ctx in every /api/chat call: modify the Archytas Ollama model adapter to include num_ctx in request options"
      - "Set OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=64000 as an Ollama server environment variable (applies globally to all /api/chat calls)"
      - "Bake num_ctx into the Modelfile: add 'PARAMETER num_ctx 64000' to each model's Modelfile"
      - "Add Ollama log monitoring: parse Ollama logs for 'truncating input prompt' warnings and flag in experiment results"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 4: Data / Configuration Path Errors
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "4A"
    category: "data_path"
    name: "FileNotFoundError — Incorrect Data Path in Container"
    description: |
      The LLM (or the code it generates) tries to access a file path that does
      not exist inside the container. Causes include: incorrect path in config
      YAML (e.g., /data/... instead of data/...), Beaker kernel cwd not set to
      /workspace, or LLM generating an absolute path that doesn't match the
      container's mount structure.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "FileNotFoundError"
        - "No such file or directory"
      trace_regex:

Both edits are done. Now let me lay out the context size discussion.

---

## Context Size Issues: What's Actually Happening and How to Fix It

### Recap of the Two Distinct Problems

**Issue 1 (3E): Beaker kernel state serialization blows up the context — pony-alpha**

The model called `bdi.match_schema(df_subset, target="gdc", method="similarity_flooding")` in turn 2. This loaded the entire GDC schema vocabulary into the Python kernel as live Python objects. After each turn, Beaker runs `FETCH_STATE_CODE` (defined in `beaker_kernel/subkernels/python.py` lines 27–124), which introspects **every variable in the kernel** and serializes it to JSON. That serialized blob became ~1M tokens. It gets injected into the messages sent to the LLM, and — boom — 5x the 200K context window.

**Issue 2 (3H): Ollama ignores the configured context length**

`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000` in `.env` is only used by `exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh` for the pre-load `/api/generate` call. When Archytas sends subsequent `/api/chat` requests, it doesn't pass `num_ctx`, so Ollama defaults to 4096. Every Ollama-based run has been operating with an effective 4096-token context window. For qwen3-coder, 99.4% of the prompt was silently discarded.

---

### Your Question: Doesn't Archytas Auto-Summarize?

**Yes, it does.** Archytas has two mechanisms:

1. **Proactive summarization**: After each turn, it checks `needs_summarization()` — if estimated tokens exceed 50% of the model's context window, it summarizes older conversation turns into a compressed `SummaryRecord`.

2. **Reactive summarization**: If the LLM API raises `ContextWindowExceededError`, Archytas catches it, triggers `summarize_history()`, waits for it, then retries the LLM call with compressed history.

**But here's why it didn't help for either issue:**

- **For Issue 1 (pony-alpha):** The problem is not the *conversation history* being too long — it's the **kernel state from a single turn** being too large. `FETCH_STATE_CODE` serializes the GDC schema (~1M tokens) and Beaker injects it into the current message context. Archytas's summarizer compresses *prior turns*, but it cannot compress the current turn's payload. Even if you summarized all prior history down to zero, the kernel state alone exceeds the context window. The summarizer was never designed to handle this — it's a different layer entirely.

- **For Issue 2 (Ollama):** Archytas *thinks* it's sending the right amount of tokens (it estimates tokens against the model's declared context window). But Ollama silently enforces a hard `num_ctx=4096` limit at the server level, completely bypassing Archytas's token accounting. Archytas has no way to know this is happening — there's no error, no exception, just silent truncation in the Ollama log.

### How Does the GDC Schema Get FULLY LOADED?

The `bdi.match_schema()` call (from the BDI library) performs similarity flooding, which requires loading the full target schema vocabulary into memory as Python data structures — dictionaries, lists, DataFrames. These become regular Python variables in the Beaker kernel namespace. Then `FETCH_STATE_CODE` walks through *every* variable via `locals()` and serializes them. It does have some limits (99 items per collection, `.head()` for DataFrames), but:

- The GDC schema is structured as deeply nested dicts/lists, not a single flat DataFrame
- Each nested dict gets fully serialized
- The 99-item truncation only applies to top-level collections, not nested structures
- The total serialized output balloons because the schema has thousands of fields across hundreds of nested objects

---

### Approaches to Fix These

Here are the options, organized by which issue they address:

#### Fix for Issue 2 (Ollama num_ctx) — Quick Win

This one is straightforward and should be done first:

**Option A: Set `OLLAMA_NUM_CTX` as a server environment variable.** In `exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh`, when launching Ollama, export `OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=64000`. This makes Ollama apply the context length globally to all `/api/chat` calls, regardless of what the client sends. This is a 1-line change.

**Option B: Modify the Archytas Ollama adapter.** Find where Archytas constructs the `/api/chat` request and add `"num_ctx": 64000` to the options payload. More correct but requires touching library code.

I'd recommend **Option A** — it's a single env var in the startup script, zero risk.

#### Fix for Issue 1 (Kernel State Explosion) — The Hard One

This is where the design question gets interesting. There are several layers at which you could intervene:

**Layer 1: Prevent the problem at source (Beaker's FETCH_STATE_CODE)**

- **Cap total serialized state size.** Add a byte/token budget to `FETCH_STATE_CODE`. If the total serialized JSON exceeds, say, 50K characters, stop adding variables and append a `"_truncation_warning": "State exceeded budget, 47 variables omitted"`.
- **Exclude large variables.** After serialization, measure each variable's JSON size and drop any single variable exceeding a threshold (e.g., 10K chars). Replace with a placeholder like `"<large object: 847KB, type=dict>"`.
- **Blacklist known offenders.** If `bdi` objects are always huge, specifically exclude variables of certain types from serialization.

This is the simplest fix and addresses the root cause. It's a modification to `FETCH_STATE_CODE` in the Beaker subkernel.

**Layer 2: Pre-flight token budget check (between Beaker and Archytas)**

- Before sending the LLM request, estimate the total token count (system prompt + history + current message including kernel state). If it exceeds N% of the model's context window, truncate or refuse.
- This would require a new piece of logic — either in `run_experiment.py` or as a wrapper around the Archytas `execute()` call.

**Layer 3: Context compression strategies (Archytas level)**

- **Middle-out truncation**: Drop the middle of the conversation, keeping the system prompt + first turn + last N turns. OpenRouter actually offers this as a parameter (`transforms: ["middle-out"]`).
- **Conversation compaction**: Summarize the entire conversation to a fixed token budget before each LLM call (not just when exceeding threshold).
- **Sliding window**: Only send the last N turns plus a summary of everything before.

These are more architectural and would require a custom module.

---

### Should We Make a Separate Module?

Here's how I'd think about it:

- **The Ollama num_ctx fix (Issue 2)**: No module needed. 1-line env var change in `exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh`.

- **The kernel state size cap (Issue 1, Layer 1)**: This is a modification to `FETCH_STATE_CODE` in the Beaker package. You'd either:
  - Patch the installed package in `.venv/` (fragile, lost on reinstall)
  - Fork/override the subkernel code in your own codebase
  - Or contribute upstream to Beaker

- **A context budget manager (Issue 1, Layers 2–3)**: This *could* warrant a separate module if you want sophisticated strategies (middle-out, compaction, sliding window). But I'd argue you should try Layer 1 first — if capping the serialized state at a reasonable size (say, 50K chars) prevents the GDC schema from being dumped into context, the Archytas auto-summarizer should handle the rest normally.

**My recommended order:**
1. Fix Issue 2 with `OLLAMA_NUM_CTX` env var (5 minutes)
2. Fix Issue 1 at Layer 1 by capping `FETCH_STATE_CODE` output size (the kernel state serialization is the actual root cause)
3. Only if step 2 is insufficient, build a context budget module at Layer 2/3

What's your thinking? Do you want to go Layer 1 first, or do you feel the deeper context management (Layer 2/3) is needed regardless? And for the Beaker `FETCH_STATE_CODE` — do you want to patch it in `.venv/` directly, or maintain a custom override in your codebase?

   562→            )
   563→        return super().execute(additional_messages, tools=self.tools)

   587→    def retrieve_summarized_messages_of_summary(
   588→        self,
   589→        summary_record_uuid: str,
   590→        agent_ref: AgentRef,
   591→    ) -> str:
   592→        """
   593→        Temporarily retrieves and rehydrates the full, raw contents of the messages summarized by the referenced record.
   594→        The contents will be available during the current ReAct loop, but will be removed once the current loop is
   595→        finished.
   596→
   597→        Args:
   598→            summary_record_uuid (str): The UUID value of the summary record from which you want to recover the
   599→                    full, unsummarized messages.
   600→
   601→        Returns:
   602→            str: The full contents of the requested previously summarized messages.
   603→"""
   604→        from typing import cast
   605→        agent = cast(ReActAgent, agent_ref)
   606→        summary: SummaryRecord
   607→
   608→        summary = next(
   609→            (
   610→                summary_record for summary_record
   611→                in agent.chat_history.summaries
   612→                if summary_record.uuid == summary_record_uuid
   613→                or summary_record_uuid in summary_record.summarized_messages
   614→            ),
   615→            None
   616→        )
   617→
   618→        if not summary:
   619→            return f"Error: Unable to locate summary {summary_record_uuid}"
   620→
   621→        # This method of collecting records should ensure correct ordering
   622→        summarized_records: list[MessageRecord[BaseMessage]] = [
   623→            message_record for message_record
   624→            in agent.chat_history.raw_records
   625→            if message_record.uuid in summary.summarized_messages
   626→        ]
   627→
   628→        if len(summarized_records) != len(summary.summarized_messages):
   629→            return f"Error: Unable to retrieve all messages from summary {summary.uuid}"
   630→
   631→        if not summarized_records:
   632→            all_summaries = [
   633→                (summary_record.uuid, summary_record.summarized_messages)
   634→                for summary_record in agent.chat_history.summaries
   635→            ]
   636→            if all_summaries:
   637→                summary_text = "\n".join([f"  Summary `{summary_uuid}`:\n    Message uuids: {', '.join(messages)}" for summary_uuid, messages in all_summaries])
   638→            else:
   639→                summary_text = "  No summaries exist."
   640→            response = f"""\
   641→Error: Unable to locate a the requested records.
   642→Available summaries are:
   643→    {summary_text}
   644→"""

   202→        """Remove all context messages from the agent's conversation."""
   203→        from .chat_history import MessageRecord
   204→        to_remove = []
   205→        for index, record in enumerate(self.chat_history.raw_records):

   212→    def set_auto_context(

   215→        content_updater: Callable[[], str] | None = None,
   216→        auto_update: bool = True,
   217→    ):
   218→        """
   219→        A special type of context message that is always towards the top (but after the prompt and any system messages).
   220→        This allows an agent to automatically update its context based on live conditions without having to call a tool every time.
   221→
   222→        Args:
   223→            default_content (str): The default message/content of the context if the content updater has not or cannot be run.
   224→            content_updater (callable): A function/lambda that takes no arguments and returns a string. The returned string
   225→                                        becomes the new context value.
   226→            auto_update (boolean): If true, the context will be updated on every call. Otherwise, the context can be updated by
   227→                                   calling `chat_history.auto_context_message.update_content()` when desired.
   228→        """
   229→        self.chat_history.auto_update_context = auto_update
   230→        self.chat_history.auto_context_message = AutoContextMessage(

   232→            content_updater=content_updater,

+    name: "Model Pre-load Timeout (Beaker Never Started)"
+    description: |
+      The Ollama model pre-loading step in exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh exceeds the
+      MAX_WAIT timeout (default 300s). The pre-load curl to /api/generate blocks

+      3. GPU contention: two SLURM GPU jobs land on the same node/GPU, and the

+      This is a SILENT degradation — Ollama still produces output, but the model

+      - "Add Ollama log monitoring: parse Ollama logs for 'truncating input prompt' warnings and flag in experiment results"
+

    """Wait for Beaker server to be ready."""
    import urllib.request
    import urllib.error

    start_time = time.time()
    check_url = f"{server_url}/api/sessions"

    print(f"Waiting for Beaker server to be ready (up to {timeout}s)...")
    print("  (Local LLM model loading can take 2-4 minutes)")

    while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
        try:

                headers={"Authorization": f"token {token}"}
            )
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5) as response:

                    return True

    if not self.is_connected:

### 1. FETCH_STATE_CODE in beaker_kernel/subkernels/python.py

**File:** `/hpc/compgen/projects/llm_GEO_project/harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/beaker_kernel/subkernels/python.py`

**Lines:** 27-124

#### What It Serializes:
The `FETCH_STATE_CODE` is a multi-line Python string (lines 27-124) that, when executed in the kernel, returns a dictionary with four categories:

```python
{
    "modules": {},      # All imported modules with path and full name
    "variables": {},    # All local variables with type, size, and value
    "functions": {},    # All defined functions with docstring and signature
    "classes": {}       # All defined classes with docstring
}
```

#### Structure Details:

**Modules (lines 65-74):**
- Captured: `module.__file__`, `module.__name__`
- Format: `{module_name: {"path": str, "full_name": str}}`

**Variables (lines 76-115):**
- Captured: value, type, size (shape or len), truncation flag
- Truncation rules (lines 94-107):
  - DataFrames: `.head()` (first 5 rows)
  - Sequences: `[:99]` (first 99 items)
  - Serialization: value converted to JSON via custom `_SubkernelStateEncoder`

**Functions (lines 60-64):**
- Captured: `docstring`, `signature`
- Format: `{function_name: {"docstring": str, "signature": str}}`

**Classes (lines 56-58):**
- Captured: `docstring` only
- Format: `{class_name: {"docstring": str}}`

#### Truncation Mechanism:
- **Line 78-82**: Skips recursion on `globals()` and `locals()` themselves
- **Line 96-107**: For large data structures:
  - First tries `.head()` (pandas DataFrames)
  - Then tries `[:99]` slice (sequences)
  - Sets `truncated: True` flag if content exceeds bounds
- **Line 119**: Final JSON serialization with fallback encoder that stringifies non-JSON-serializable objects

#### Error Handling:
- **Lines 116-117**: Logs warnings for individual variable failures (doesn't fail the whole fetch)
- **Lines 120-122**: Catches serialization errors, returns empty dict instead of crashing

#### Maximum Size:
No explicit size limit is enforced. The truncation is **length-based** (99 items or first 5 rows), not byte-size-based. Large variables that fit within JSON serialization will be fully included.

#### What It Serializes:
The `FETCH_STATE_CODE` is a multi-line Python string (lines 27-124) that, when executed in the kernel, returns a dictionary with four categories:

```python
{
    "modules": {},      # All imported modules with path and full name
    "variables": {},    # All local variables with type, size, and value
    "functions": {},    # All defined functions with docstring and signature
    "classes": {}       # All defined classes with docstring
}
```

#### Structure Details:

**Modules (lines 65-74):**
- Captured: `module.__file__`, `module.__name__`
- Format: `{module_name: {"path": str, "full_name": str}}`

**Variables (lines 76-115):**
- Captured: value, type, size (shape or len), truncation flag
- Truncation rules (lines 94-107):
  - DataFrames: `.head()` (first 5 rows)
  - Sequences: `[:99]` (first 99 items)
  - Serialization: value converted to JSON via custom `_SubkernelStateEncoder`

**Functions (lines 60-64):**
- Captured: `docstring`, `signature`
- Format: `{function_name: {"docstring": str, "signature": str}}`

**Classes (lines 56-58):**
- Captured: `docstring` only
- Format: `{class_name: {"docstring": str}}`

#### Truncation Mechanism:
- **Line 78-82**: Skips recursion on `globals()` and `locals()` themselves
- **Line 96-107**: For large data structures:
  - First tries `.head()` (pandas DataFrames)
  - Then tries `[:99]` slice (sequences)
  - Sets `truncated: True` flag if content exceeds bounds
- **Line 119**: Final JSON serialization with fallback encoder that stringifies non-JSON-serializable objects

#### Error Handling:
- **Lines 116-117**: Logs warnings for individual variable failures (doesn't fail the whole fetch)
- **Lines 120-122**: Catches serialization errors, returns empty dict instead of crashing

#### Maximum Size:
No explicit size limit is enforced. The truncation is **length-based** (99 items or first 5 rows), not byte-size-based. Large variables that fit within JSON serialization will be fully included.

  Comprehensive survey reviewing memory module design and evaluation for LLM-based agents. Categorizes approaches into retrieval-based, summarization-based, and KV cache compression.

- **[Adaptive Focus Memory for Language Models (arXiv:2511.12712)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12712)**
  Allocates each past message to one of three fidelity levels (FULL, COMPRESSED, or PLACEHOLDER) to preserve salient information while minimizing prompt length. Directly relevant to conversation context management.

- **[How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study (arXiv:2505.16067)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16067)**
  Empirical study of experience-following behavior in LLM agents as affected by memory management strategies.

---

## 3. GitHub Repos / Tools Implementing Context Management

### LangChain

- **[ConversationSummaryBufferMemory - LangChain Docs](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/langchain/memory/langchain.memory.summary_buffer.ConversationSummaryBufferMemory.html)**
  Hybrid of summary + buffer memory: summarizes the earliest interactions while maintaining the most recent tokens in raw form. Key parameter: `max_token_limit` (default 2000). Note: deprecated since v0.3.1, migration guide available.

- **[Conversational Memory for LLMs with LangChain (Pinecone)](https://www.pinecone.io/learn/series/langchain/langchain-conversational-memory/)**
  Tutorial covering all LangChain memory types: ConversationBufferMemory, ConversationBufferWindowMemory, ConversationSummaryMemory, and ConversationSummaryBufferMemory with practical examples.

### LlamaIndex

- **[Memory | LlamaIndex Python Documentation](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/deploying/agents/memory/)**
  Documents three memory types: ChatMemoryBuffer (last X messages within token limit), ChatSummaryMemoryBuffer (periodic summarization when conversation gets too long), and VectorMemory (retrieval from vector DB by semantic similarity).

- **[Chat Engine - Context Mode | LlamaIndex](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/examples/chat_engine/chat_engine_context/)**
  Retrieves context via a retriever, sets it in the system prompt, and uses the LLM for response generation. Configurable with `ChatMemoryBuffer.from_defaults(token_limit=1500)`.

- **[Chat Engine - Condense Plus Context Mode | LlamaIndex](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/examples/chat_engine/chat_engine_condense_plus_context/)**
  Condensation strategy that rewrites the user's query using conversation history before retrieving context. Combines summarization with retrieval.

### MemGPT / Letta

- **[GitHub: letta-ai/letta (formerly MemGPT)](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta)**
  Open-source agent framework implementing virtual context management with two-tier memory (core memory in-context + archival memory in external storage). LLM autonomously manages memory operations via function calls.

- **[Letta Documentation - MemGPT Concepts](https://docs.letta.com/concepts/memgpt/)**
  Explains MemGPT as the agent design pattern with two tiers of memory, now part of the Letta framework as of September 2024.

- **[Letta Documentation - Research Background](https://docs.letta.com/concepts/letta/)**
  Research background on the Letta framework and how it evolved from the MemGPT paper.

### LLMLingua (Microsoft)

- **[GitHub: microsoft/LLMLingua](https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua)**
  Official implementation of LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, and LLMLingua-2. Achieves up to 20x prompt compression with minimal performance loss. Published at EMNLP 2023 and ACL 2024.

### Beaker / Archytas

- **[GitHub: jataware/beaker-kernel](https://github.com/jataware/beaker-kernel)**
  Contextually-aware notebooks with built-in AI assistant. Powered by Archytas. Contexts provide behind-the-scenes functionality including custom data loaders, specialized tools, and customized LLM prompts.

- **[GitHub: jataware/archytas](https://github.com/jataware/archytas)**
  LLM agent framework powering Beaker. Manages ReAct decision loops and tool integration. No specific public PRs/issues were found for context window management or conversation truncation -- this appears to be an area where custom implementation would be needed.

### Other Relevant Repos / Tools

- **[GitHub: Shichun-Liu/Agent-Memory-Paper-List](https://github.com/Shichun-Liu/Agent-Memory-Paper-List)**
  Curated paper list from the survey "Memory in the Age of AI Agents." Useful as a comprehensive bibliography for memory-related research.

- **[Context Window Management | Roo-Code DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/RooCodeInc/Roo-Code/7.3-context-window-management)**
  Documentation of how Roo-Code (coding agent) manages context windows, including integration with OpenRouter's middle-out transform.

---

## 4. Ollama Documentation

- **[FAQ - Ollama](https://docs.ollama.com/faq)**
  Official FAQ covering context window configuration. Default context window is 4096 tokens. Can be set via `num_ctx` parameter in API requests or via the `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` environment variable when starting Ollama from the command line. Note: the env var is `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`, not `OLLAMA_NUM_CTX`.

- **[Ollama Context Length: Default Settings and How to Modify (Deep AI)](https://deepai.tn/glossary/ollama/ollama-context-length/)**
  Comprehensive guide on `num_ctx` behavior: the context length includes both input and output tokens. Larger `num_ctx` increases VRAM/RAM usage and inference time. Increasing beyond the training maximum can degrade output quality.

- **[Ollama run silently truncating prompt (GitHub Issue #8099)](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/8099)**
  Documents the silent truncation problem: when a prompt exceeds `num_ctx`, Ollama trims from the start of the prompt without warning the user. This means if the prompt starts with a question, that question is never sent to the model.

- **[Chat history and embedding truncation happens silently (GitHub Issue #14259)](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/14259)**
  Reports that conversation truncation happens silently with no user-visible indication. When token count exceeds context length, Ollama silently drops older messages from the front of the conversation.

- **[OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH env var vs num_ctx (GitHub Issue #10829)](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/10829)**
  Documents a bug where `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384` is set but Ollama runs with `--ctx-size 4096`. Shows the disconnect between environment variable configuration and actual runtime behavior.

- **[num_ctx in practice is proven to be unstable and useless (GitHub Issue #10974)](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/10974)**
  Community report of instability with the `num_ctx` parameter in practice.

- **[ragflow get ollama api warn: truncating input prompt (GitHub Issue #10368)](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/10368)**
  Shows the runner.go warning in practice: `level=WARN source=runner.go:129 msg="truncating input prompt" limit=2048`. The warning includes fields for `limit`, `prompt`, `keep`, and `new` which indicate how the truncation is being applied.

- **[Ollama endpoints options parameter (Medium)](https://medium.com/@laurentkubaski/ollama-model-options-0eee31c902d3)**
  Practical guide to Ollama's model options including `num_ctx`, covering both CLI usage (`/set parameter num_ctx 4096`) and API usage.

- **[Setting Parameters like Context Length and Temperature in Ollama Models](https://www.tspi.at/2025/08/10/ollamaparams.html)**
  Practical guide covering how to set `num_ctx` via Modelfile, CLI, API options, and environment variables, with discussion of per-model defaults.

---

## Supplementary General References

- **[Context Window Management: Strategies for Long-Context AI Agents and Chatbots (Maxim)](https://www.getmaxim.ai/articles/context-window-management-strategies-for-long-context-ai-agents-and-chatbots/)**
  Broad overview of context management strategies including truncation, summarization, RAG, sliding windows, and hybrid approaches. Good introductory reference.

- **[Top Techniques to Manage Context Lengths in LLMs (Agenta)](https://agenta.ai/blog/top-6-techniques-to-manage-context-length-in-llms)**
  Practical taxonomy of six techniques for managing context length.

- **[Conversation Management - Strands Agents](https://strandsagents.com/latest/documentation/docs/user-guide/concepts/agents/conversation-management/)**
  Documents SlidingWindowConversationManager (fixed window, removes oldest messages) and SummarizingConversationManager (summarizes older messages instead of discarding). Good reference implementation patterns.

- **[LLM Powered Autonomous Agents (Lil'Log - Lilian Weng)](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-06-23-agent/)**
  Foundational blog post on LLM agent architectures, including memory components. Widely cited reference for agent system design.

# Context Management Between Beaker and Archytas

**Date:** 25 February 2026
**Purpose:** Comprehensive reference on how context flows between the Beaker kernel and Archytas agent framework, where intervention points exist, and what strategies are available for managing context size.

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Architecture Overview](#1-architecture-overview)
2. [Beaker: Kernel State Serialization (FETCH_STATE_CODE)](#2-beaker-kernel-state-serialization)
3. [Beaker → Archytas: The Auto-Context Bridge](#3-beaker--archytas-the-auto-context-bridge)
4. [Archytas: Message Accumulation & Chat History](#4-archytas-message-accumulation--chat-history)
5. [Archytas: Summarization System](#5-archytas-summarization-system)
6. [Archytas → LLM: Model Adapters & Token Accounting](#6-archytas--llm-model-adapters--token-accounting)
7. [Ollama: Context Length Configuration](#7-ollama-context-length-configuration)
8. [Intervention Points for Context Size Control](#8-intervention-points-for-context-size-control)
9. [Context Management Strategies (Literature & Practice)](#9-context-management-strategies)
10. [References](#10-references)

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        EXPERIMENT FLOW                              │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Python Kernel │───>│   Beaker     │───>│      Archytas          │ │
│  │ (Jupyter)     │    │   Server     │    │   (Agent Framework)    │ │
│  │               │    │              │    │                        │ │
│  │ - Variables   │    │ - Runs       │    │ - Chat History         │ │
│  │ - Modules     │    │   FETCH_     │    │ - Summarization        │ │
│  │ - Functions   │    │   STATE_CODE │    │ - Token Estimation     │ │
│  │ - Classes     │    │ - Formats as │    │ - ReAct Loop           │ │
│  │               │    │   auto_ctx   │    │                        │ │
│  └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘    └────────┬───────────────┘ │
│                                                    │                 │
│                                          ┌────────▼───────────────┐ │
│                                          │   LLM Provider API     │ │
│                                          │                        │ │
│                                          │ - Ollama /api/chat     │ │
│                                          │ - OpenRouter            │ │
│                                          │ - OpenAI               │ │
│                                          └────────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Data Flow Per Turn

```
1. User/Automation sends message
       │
2. Beaker executes FETCH_STATE_CODE in kernel
       │ Returns: {modules, variables, functions, classes} as JSON
       │
3. Beaker formats state as Markdown + JSON code block (auto_context)
       │
4. Archytas assembles message list:
       │   [system_prompt, auto_context, summaries, raw_messages]
       │
5. Archytas estimates tokens
       │   If > summarization_threshold → trigger summarization
       │
6. Archytas sends messages to LLM via model adapter
       │   (ChatOllama, OpenAI, etc.)
       │
7. LLM responds → Archytas records in chat_history
       │
8. If ReAct loop: execute tool calls → kernel runs code → go to step 2
       │
9. Post-loop: summarize tool outputs if large
```

---

## 2. Beaker: Kernel State Serialization

### FETCH_STATE_CODE

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/beaker_kernel/subkernels/python.py` (lines 27–124)

This is a Python code string that Beaker executes *inside the Jupyter kernel* after each turn. It introspects the kernel namespace and returns a JSON dictionary.

### What It Serializes

```python
_result = {
    "modules": {},      # Imported modules: {name: {path, full_name}}
    "variables": {},    # User variables: {name: {value, type, size, truncated?}}
    "functions": {},    # Defined functions: {name: {docstring, signature}}
    "classes": {}       # Defined classes: {name: {docstring}}
}
```

### Existing Truncation Rules

| Data Type | Truncation | Lines |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| DataFrames | `.head()` (first 5 rows) | ~96–99 |
| Sequences (list, tuple, set) | First 99 items, `truncated: True` flag | ~100–107 |
| Private vars (`_name`) | Skipped entirely | ~78 |
| Builtins (`In`, `Out`, etc.) | Skipped | ~80–82 |
| Non-serializable objects | Stringified via `_SubkernelStateEncoder` | ~119 |

### What Is NOT Limited

- **Total output size**: No byte/character budget. If 50 variables each serialize to 20KB, the total is 1MB.
- **Individual variable size**: A single dict with 10,000 nested entries will be fully serialized (only top-level collections are truncated to 99 items).
- **Nested structures**: The 99-item limit applies only at the top level. A dict with 5 keys, each containing a list of 100,000 items, passes through.
- **String values**: No character limit on string variable values.

### The GDC Schema Problem

When `bdi.match_schema(df, target="gdc", method="similarity_flooding")` runs, it loads the full GDC schema vocabulary into kernel memory as deeply nested Python dicts/lists. These become regular variables in `locals()`. FETCH_STATE_CODE serializes them all, producing ~1M tokens of JSON. The 99-item truncation doesn't help because:
- The schema is structured as nested dicts, not flat lists
- Each top-level key maps to a complex nested object
- The encoder faithfully serializes all nested content

---

## 3. Beaker → Archytas: The Auto-Context Bridge

### State Retrieval

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/beaker_kernel/lib/context.py` (lines 460–465)

```python
async def get_subkernel_state(self):
    fetch_state_code = self.subkernel.FETCH_STATE_CODE
    state = await self.evaluate(fetch_state_code)
    for warning in state["stderr_list"]:
        logger.warning(warning)
    return state["return"]
```

### Auto-Context Formatting

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/beaker_kernel/lib/context.py` (lines 210–252)

```python
async def auto_context(self):
    parts = []
    # ... other context parts ...
    if beaker_config.send_kernel_state:
        kernel_state = await self.get_subkernel_state()
        if kernel_state:
            parts.append(f"""## Kernel state
```application/json
{json.dumps(kernel_state)}
```""")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)
```

The serialized kernel state becomes a **Markdown section with an embedded JSON code block**. This entire string becomes a single `AutoContextMessage` in Archytas.

### Registration with Archytas

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/agent.py` (lines 212–234)

```python
self.chat_history.auto_context_message = AutoContextMessage(
    default_content=default_content,
    content_updater=content_updater,  # ← The auto_context() callable
    model=self.model,
)
```

The `AutoContextMessage` is:
- Updated **before every LLM call** via `update_content()`
- Positioned **after the system prompt, before conversation history**
- A `SystemMessage` subclass — it is NOT subject to summarization

---

## 4. Archytas: Message Accumulation & Chat History

### ChatHistory Structure

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/chat_history.py` (lines 126–182)

```python
class ChatHistory:
    raw_records: list[MessageRecord]          # All messages
    summaries: list[SummaryRecord]            # Compressed message groups
    system_message: Optional[MessageRecord]   # System prompt
    auto_context_message: Optional[AutoContextMessage]  # Kernel state
    summarization_threshold: int              # Token trigger
    tool_token_estimate: int                  # Tool definitions size
    base_tokens: int                          # Overhead
```

### Message List Assembly

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/chat_history.py` (lines 393–420)

`records()` returns messages in this order:

```
1. system_message           (SystemMessage — never summarized)
2. auto_context_message     (AutoContextMessage — never summarized)
3. summaries                (SummaryRecord — compressed prior turns)
4. user_preamble            (if present)
5. raw_records              (unsummarized recent messages)
```

### Message Recording

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/chat_history.py` (lines 459–467)

```python
def add_message(self, message, token_count=None):
    record = MessageRecord(
        message=message,
        token_count=token_count,
        react_loop_id=self.current_loop_id
    )
    self.raw_records.append(record)
    return record
```

---

## 5. Archytas: Summarization System

### Two-Tier Summarization

#### Tier 1: Loop Summarization (Tool Outputs)

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/summarizers.py` (lines 84–105)

After each ReAct loop, tool outputs exceeding `MESSAGE_SUMMARIZATION_THRESHOLD` (1000 chars) are truncated to the first 1000 characters.

#### Tier 2: History Summarization (Conversation Compression)

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/summarizers.py` (lines 108–177)

When total tokens exceed the summarization threshold, the oldest messages are bundled and sent to the LLM for summarization. The LLM produces a compressed `SummaryRecord` that replaces those messages.

### Summarization Threshold

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/models/base.py` (lines 121–144)

```python
DEFAULT_SUMMARIZATION_RATIO = 0.5  # 50% of context window

@property
def summarization_threshold(self):
    context_size = self.contextsize(self.model_name)
    # Use explicit threshold, percentage, or default 50%
    return int(context_size * summarization_ratio)
```

### What Gets Summarized vs. What Doesn't

| Message Type | Summarized? |
|-------------|------------|
| System prompt | Never |
| AutoContextMessage (kernel state) | **Never** |
| SummaryRecords (already summarized) | Never |
| User messages | Yes |
| Assistant messages | Yes |
| Tool call/result messages | Yes (after loop summarization) |

### ContextWindowExceededError Recovery

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/react.py` (lines 519–529)

```python
except ContextWindowExceededError:
    history_summarization_task = self.chat_history.history_summarization_task
    if not history_summarization_task:
        history_summarization_task = await self.chat_history.summarize_history(
            agent=self, in_loop=True
        )
    if history_summarization_task:
        await history_summarization_task
    reaction = await self.execute()  # Retry with compressed history
```

### Why Summarization Doesn't Fix the GDC Schema Problem

The auto-context message (containing serialized kernel state) is a `SystemMessage` subtype and is **excluded from summarization**. Even if all conversation history were summarized to zero tokens, the auto-context alone can be ~1M tokens — exceeding the entire context window. Archytas's summarizer operates on *conversation history*, not on the *kernel state payload*.

---

## 6. Archytas → LLM: Model Adapters & Token Accounting

### Ollama Adapter

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/models/ollama.py`

```python
# Context size discovery (lines 36-48)
@lru_cache()
def contextsize(self, model_name=None):
    show_response = self.model._client.show(self.model_name)
    model_info = show_response.modelinfo
    model_arch = model_info["general.architecture"]
    context_length = model_info[f"{model_arch}.context_length"]
    return int(context_length)
```

### ChatOllama (LangChain-Ollama)

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/langchain_ollama/chat_models.py`

```python
# num_ctx field definition (lines 572-576)
num_ctx: int | None = None  # Default: None → Ollama uses its own default (4096)

# Chat params building (lines 717-785)
def _chat_params(self, messages, stop=None, **kwargs):
    options_dict = {
        "num_ctx": self.num_ctx,  # ← Only sent if set on instance
        # ... other options ...
    }
    params = {
        "messages": ollama_messages,
        "options": options_dict,
        # ...
    }
```

**Key finding:** `num_ctx` is only included in `/api/chat` requests if explicitly set on the `ChatOllama` instance. By default it's `None`, which means Ollama falls back to 4096.

### Token Estimation

**File:** `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/archytas/chat_history.py` (lines 317–391)

```python
token_estimate = (
    base_tokens +
    tool_token_estimate +
    auto_context_message_token_estimate +
    sum(record.token_count for record in records)
)
```

**Note:** For Ollama models, `get_num_tokens_from_messages()` is not accurately implemented — it returns approximate counts. Actual usage comes from response metadata.

---

## 7. Ollama: Context Length Configuration

### The num_ctx Disconnect

There are **three separate places** where context length can be configured for Ollama, and they don't propagate to each other:

```
1. OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH in .env
   → Read by exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh
   → Passed to /api/generate (pre-load only)
   → NOT passed to /api/chat

2. ChatOllama(num_ctx=N)
   → Passed to /api/chat via options dict
   → NOT set by Harmonia's codebase (defaults to None → 4096)

3. OLLAMA_NUM_CTX environment variable
   → Read by Ollama server at startup
   → Applies globally to all /api/chat calls
   → NOT currently set by exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh
```

### Ollama's Default Behavior

- Default `num_ctx` = 4096 tokens
- When prompt exceeds `num_ctx`, Ollama **silently truncates** from the start
- Warning only appears in Ollama's own log: `msg="truncating input prompt" limit=4096 prompt=N`
- No error is raised, no exception — the LLM just receives a clipped prompt

### Relevant Ollama Source

The truncation happens in `runner.go` (Ollama's Go codebase). The warning includes:
- `limit`: the `num_ctx` value
- `prompt`: total tokens in the incoming prompt
- `keep`: tokens preserved at the start (system prompt protection)
- `new`: resulting prompt size after truncation

---

## 8. Intervention Points for Context Size Control

```
                    INTERVENTION POINTS

[Python Kernel]
    │
    ▼
[FETCH_STATE_CODE]  ◄─── POINT A: Cap serialized state size
    │                     - Per-variable size limit
    │                     - Total budget limit
    │                     - Type-based blacklisting
    ▼
[BeakerContext.auto_context()]  ◄─── POINT B: Truncate auto-context
    │                                 - Measure JSON size before embedding
    │                                 - Drop large sections
    ▼
[ChatHistory.records()]  ◄─── POINT C: Pre-flight token check
    │                          - Estimate total before sending
    │                          - Refuse if over budget
    ▼
[Agent.execute()]  ◄─── POINT D: Archytas summarization
    │                    - Already exists (50% threshold)
    │                    - Cannot compress auto-context
    ▼
[Model.ainvoke()]  ◄─── POINT E: Model adapter config
    │                    - Pass num_ctx for Ollama
    │                    - Use middle-out for OpenRouter
    ▼
[Ollama /api/chat]  ◄─── POINT F: Server-level config
                          - OLLAMA_NUM_CTX env var
                          - Per-model Modelfile
```

### Which Points Address Which Problems

| Problem | Root Cause | Best Intervention Point |
|---------|-----------|------------------------|
| Ollama silent truncation (3H) | num_ctx not passed | **Point E** (model adapter) or **Point F** (env var) |
| GDC schema explosion (3E) | Kernel state too large | **Point A** (FETCH_STATE_CODE) |
| Gradual context growth | Conversation history accumulates | **Point D** (already handled by Archytas) |
| Large tool outputs | Code execution returns large data | **Point D** (loop summarization, 1000 char limit) |

---

## 9. Context Management Strategies

### Strategy 1: Truncation (Drop Oldest)

Remove the oldest messages from conversation history, keeping only the N most recent turns plus the system prompt.

**Pros:** Simple, deterministic, no LLM calls needed.
**Cons:** Loses important early context (task description, initial data exploration).

**Implementations:**
- LangChain `ConversationBufferWindowMemory` (keeps last k turns)
- Strands Agents `SlidingWindowConversationManager`

### Strategy 2: Summarization (Compress History)

Use the LLM itself to summarize older conversation turns into a compact representation.

**Pros:** Preserves semantic content, context-aware compression.
**Cons:** Costs LLM calls, may lose details, adds latency.

**Implementations:**
- Archytas built-in `default_history_summarizer` (already present)
- LangChain `ConversationSummaryBufferMemory` (hybrid: summary + recent raw)
- LlamaIndex `ChatSummaryMemoryBuffer`
- Strands Agents `SummarizingConversationManager`

### Strategy 3: Middle-Out (Drop Middle, Keep Edges)

Remove content from the middle of the prompt, keeping the system prompt + first turns and the most recent turns. Exploits the "lost in the middle" phenomenon where LLMs attend less to middle content.

**Pros:** Preserves both initial instructions and recent state.
**Cons:** Lossy, may miss critical mid-conversation decisions.

**Implementations:**
- OpenRouter's `transforms: ["middle-out"]` parameter
- For Anthropic models: keeps first half + last half of messages (up to 1000-message limit)

### Strategy 4: Retrieval-Augmented Context (RAG)

Store all conversation history externally, retrieve only relevant portions per query using semantic similarity.

**Pros:** Scales to unlimited history, retrieves what's relevant.
**Cons:** Complex infrastructure, retrieval may miss important context.

**Implementations:**
- LlamaIndex `VectorMemory`
- MemGPT/Letta archival memory tier

### Strategy 5: Virtual Context Management (MemGPT)

Inspired by OS memory hierarchies: fast "core memory" (in-context) + slow "archival memory" (external storage). The LLM decides what to keep in-context and what to archive.

**Pros:** Self-managed, adaptive, theoretically unbounded context.
**Cons:** Complex, requires LLM to learn memory management, adds overhead.

**Implementations:**
- MemGPT/Letta (`letta-ai/letta` on GitHub)

### Strategy 6: Prompt Compression (LLMLingua)

Use a smaller model to compress the prompt tokens, removing redundant or low-information tokens while preserving semantics.

**Pros:** High compression ratios (up to 20x), works on any content.
**Cons:** Requires separate model, may distort structured data (JSON, code).

**Implementations:**
- Microsoft LLMLingua / LLMLingua-2 (`microsoft/LLMLingua` on GitHub)

### Strategy 7: State Serialization Budget (Custom — For Beaker)

Cap the serialized kernel state at a fixed byte/token budget. Drop or placeholder large variables. This is specific to the Beaker architecture where kernel state is injected into context.

**Pros:** Directly addresses the root cause for Beaker-specific explosions.
**Cons:** May lose important state info. Requires careful threshold tuning.

**Implementations:** None existing — needs custom implementation in FETCH_STATE_CODE or at the auto-context layer.

### Strategy 8: Adaptive Focus Memory

Assign each past message to a fidelity level (FULL, COMPRESSED, or PLACEHOLDER) based on relevance to the current task.

**Pros:** Flexible, preserves important messages in full.
**Cons:** Requires relevance scoring, adds complexity.

**Reference:** arXiv:2511.12712 (Adaptive Focus Memory for Language Models)

---

## 10. References

### Frontier Model Provider Documentation

- [Context Windows - Claude API Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows) — Context window sizes, context rot phenomenon, premium pricing above 200K tokens
- [Context Summarization with Realtime API (OpenAI Cookbook)](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/context_summarization_with_realtime_api) — Two strategies: context trimming and context summarization with Python implementation

- [Long Context | Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/long-context) — Gemini's up to 2M token context, context caching for static content

### Academic Papers

- [LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05736) — Up to 20x prompt compression with minimal performance loss (EMNLP 2023)
- [LongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06839) — Extension for long contexts, 21.4% performance boost with 4x fewer tokens (ACL 2024)

### GitHub Repositories

- [letta-ai/letta (formerly MemGPT)](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta) — Virtual context management with core + archival memory tiers
